newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds benefit as labour market weakens.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds benefit as labour market weakens.

text.p: *Australian bonds recoup early losses and move strongly into positive territory on unexpectedly weak jobs data for March.
*Bonds finish off their highs, but are seen as well positioned for further gains in month ahead.

Australian bonds reversed early weakness to rally strongly on the release of unexpectedly weak employment data for March, ending the day off their highs but still in positive territory and positioned for further gains.

Bonds rallied across the curve, led by the short end which reached a six week high as the data revived faint hopes of an interest rate cut, although most analysts saw it as backing the view that local rates are on hold most likely into 1998.
Employment fell by 33,900 in March, of which 30,400 were full-time jobs, against median forecasts of a 13,500 rise. The unemployment rate of 8.7 percent was in line with expectations.
HSBC Markets economists said the data "highlights the difference between the Australian and U.S. economies at present, emphasizing that we are a long way from a monetary policy tightening."

Although some profit-taking had pushed the market off the highs reached soon after the data, bonds were still seen as well positioned for further gains, as the jobs data confirmed the pace of recovery through 1997 would be moderate.
Citibank Australia economists said they had expected low inflation data later this month and next month's budget would be the catalyst for some correction in local bonds.

"These are still expected to be a broad positive, but there is the added benefit for bonds that the lift in growth so evident in the first few months of 1997 has slipped a little," they said in a commentary.
The data had reinforced their view 10-year bonds would test under 7.75 percent in the next three months, with the spread to U.S. Treasuries possibly retesting its lows of 75 basis points.

While bonds rallied on the employment data, the slim prospect of another rate cut was a negative for the Australian dollar, which dropped half a cent to be at US$0.7805/10 when the bond market closed.
In other news, the Treasury will offer A$300 million of October 2000 adjustable rate bonds at tender on Friday.
Spreads ended narrower across the baord after local rally, although off their narrowest point when spreads to U.S. short end were under 30 points and 10-year spread was challenging 100.
With short end leading as expectations of a tightening pushed out, and some talking of outside chance of rate cut, curves at steepest since June futures became active contracts.
